rvtk

rvtk is an infrastructure package for R package developers: it makes the Visualization Toolkit (VTK) available to R packages that need to link against it from C++. Your users never install VTK themselves — rvtk finds a system VTK when one is present and otherwise downloads pre-built libraries automatically at install time.

Add Imports: rvtk to your DESCRIPTION, then configure your package in one step from the package root:

rvtk::use_rvtk()

use_rvtk() writes src/Makevars, src/Makevars.win, and tools/configure.R so that the compiler and linker flags are resolved at install time via rvtk::CppFlags() and rvtk::LdFlagsFile(). Everything can also be set up by hand — the two approaches produce identical files.

Pre-built libraries are provided for macOS (arm64 and x86_64), Linux (x86_64 glibc, x86_64 musl/Alpine, and aarch64), and Windows (static or shared DLLs).

See the vignette for full details: how VTK is located on each platform (with the compatibility matrix), which VTK modules are bundled, manually writing the build files, restricting linking with the modules argument, and verifying that linking worked.

Quick start 

# Install rvtk (from CRAN, or the development version)
install.packages("rvtk")
# pak::pak("astamm/rvtk")

# From the root of your downstream package:
rvtk::use_rvtk()

Then use rvtk::CppFlags(), rvtk::LdFlags(), rvtk::LdFlagsFile(), and rvtk::VtkVersion() in your build scripts or configure when you need finer control.

Installation 

# from CRAN
install.packages("rvtk")

# development version
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("astamm/rvtk")

A system VTK installation (≥ 9.1.0) is not required: if none is found the package downloads pre-built libraries automatically.
